title: Self-selective growth of GaAs1-xBix on GaAs zinc blende/wurtzite nanowire heterostructures
authors: Rohit Yadav, Sebastian Lehmann, Vidar Flodgren, Evangelos Golias, Alexei Zakharov, Kimberly A. Dick, Anders Mikkelsen, Rainer Timm
abstract: Site-selective nanostructure growth and material incorporation at the atomic scale offer a promising pathway for engineering quantum materials and nanodevices. Here, GaAs nanowires (NWs) with an axial heterostructure of alternating zinc blende (Zb) and wurtzite (Wz) crystal phases are employed as templates for site-selective Ga and Bi overgrowth. Using X-ray photoemission electron microscopy (XPEEM) with nanoscale spatial resolution, we map elemental distribution and local chemical bonding to reveal the incorporation behavior of Bi atoms in {110} Zb and {11-20} Wz facets. Bi incorporation proceeds through an anion-exchange process, where Bi atoms replace As, forming local Ga-Bi bonds and producing a thin GaAs1-xBix shell. We observe crystal-phase-dependent Bi incorporation, with higher Bi concentration in the Zb segments than in the neighboring Wz segments within the same NW. Furthermore, the Zb segment with higher Bi content exhibits reduced susceptibility to oxidation compared with the Wz segment, resulting in increased Ga-oxide in the Wz surfaces. This study highlights GaAs NW Zb/Wz heterostructures as a template for controlled growth of GaBi and GaAs1-xBix nanostructures with tailored functionalities for quantum applications
summary: This work demonstrates the controlled, site-selective growth of $	ext{GaAs}_{1-x}	ext{Bi}_x$ shells on $	ext{GaAs}$ nanowire heterostructures containing alternating zinc blende and wurtzite phases. Using advanced electron microscopy, the researchers found that bismuth incorporation strongly depends on the crystal phase, favoring the Zb segments through an anion-exchange mechanism. This provides a pathway for engineering quantum materials with tailored functionalities.
main_problem: The study aims to engineer quantum materials by achieving site-selective nanostructure growth and material incorporation at the atomic scale.
main_result: Bi incorporation into GaAs nanowires is found to be crystal-phase-dependent, favoring the zinc blende (Zb) segments via an anion-exchange process, while the wurtzite (Wz) segments show higher susceptibility to oxidation.
method: The research utilizes X-ray photoemission electron microscopy (XPEEM) and X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) to map elemental distribution and local chemical bonding across the heterostructure.
model_or_system: The physical system consists of GaAs nanowires (NWs) with an axial heterostructure alternating between zinc blende (Zb) and wurtzite (Wz) crystal phases, which are used as templates for overgrowth.
key_observables: Elemental distribution ($	ext{Bi } 5d$, $	ext{Ga } 3d$, $	ext{As } 3d$), local chemical bonding, and crystal-phase-dependent Bi incorporation ratios.
important_parameters: The study highlights the difference in incorporation behavior between the Zb and Wz facets, and the resulting difference in oxidation susceptibility.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the assumption that the observed differences in elemental signals reflect distinct chemical incorporation mechanisms (anion exchange vs. direct growth).
figures_summary: Figures show schematic representations of the NW growth, SEM images of the grown structures, and PEEM maps illustrating the spatial distribution of Bi and Ga signals across the Zb/Wz segments.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of establishing the need for site-selective growth, detailing the experimental setup using NW templates, presenting XPEEM/XPS data comparing Zb and Wz segments, and concluding with the mechanism of Bi incorporation.
why_interesting: While the focus is on solid-state materials science, the precise control over crystal phase and atomic-scale material deposition is crucial for realizing novel quantum devices, linking to concepts of engineered quantum interfaces.
